summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease, status post kidney transplant with complications, and a history of coronary artery disease and recent subendocardial infarction, was admitted for acute periumbilical abdominal pain that occurred during hemodialysis. Concern for mesenteric ischemia prompted a CT angiogram, which revealed severe calcific atherosclerosis and narrowing of the superior mesenteric artery but no evidence of acute ischemia. His symptoms improved without intervention, and he completed a session of hemodialysis without recurrence of pain. The chest pain reported was evaluated and deemed non-acute. He was discharged in stable condition with instructions to continue medical management of vascular risk factors, adhere to his renal diet, and follow up with nephrology and cardiology.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Subendocardial infarction, subsequent episode of care
Surgical operation with transplant of whole organ causing abnormal patient reaction, or later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of operation
